items.followUp: What are intermolecular forces? Give one example involving water molecules.

rubric.why: The definition identifies these forces as attractions acting between molecules.
rubric.description: Defines intermolecular forces as attractive forces between molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing them as forces of attraction between molecules; accept either listed wording.

rubric.why: A specific example shows a type of intermolecular force and the particles between which it acts.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of an intermolecular force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as hydrogen bonding between water molecules or van der Waals forces between molecules.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces are the forces of attraction between molecules.
Hydrogen bonding between water molecules is an example.

items.followUp: Define allotropy and name two allotropes of carbon.

rubric.why: Allotropy is the occurrence of one element in multiple forms while in the same physical state.
rubric.description: Defines allotropy as the existence of an element in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an element exists in two or more different forms in the same physical state.

rubric.why: Naming a pair of allotropes gives a correct example of allotropy.
rubric.description: Names a correct pair of allotropes, such as diamond and graphite or oxygen and ozone.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both members of a valid allotropic pair.

modelAnswer: Allotropy is the property of an element to exist in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon.

items.followUp: Why does oil not mix with water?

rubric.why: The difference in polarity is central to why benzene and water do not mix.
rubric.description: Identifies benzene as non-polar and water as polar.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the polarity of both substances.

rubric.why: The solubility explanation applies the principle that substances with similar polarity dissolve in one another.
rubric.description: Explains that polar water does not dissolve non-polar benzene, consistent with the like-dissolves-like principle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for applying the like-dissolves-like principle or explicitly stating that water does not dissolve benzene because of their different polarity.

modelAnswer: Benzene is non-polar, whereas water is polar.
According to the principle “like dissolves like,” polar water does not dissolve non-polar benzene.
